explanation:
[EFFECT] Temperature has a broadly positive and monotonically rising effect on hourly bike demand: cold temperatures significantly suppress rentals, while warm temperatures boost them. The contribution climbs from around −0.9 in log space at the coldest end of the range (roughly 5–10°C) to positive values of +0.2 to +0.3 at the warmest end (roughly 29–41°C). The peak effect is seen at the highest observed temperatures, with no sign of a downturn even at very warm conditions.

[IMPORTANCE] Temperature is the 3rd most influential feature out of 9, with an importance score of 0.197 — making it a major driver of predicted demand, behind only a couple of other features. Its influence is substantial and spans a wide range of contribution values.

[RECOMMENDATION] Plan for significantly higher bike availability and staffing during warm weather, and reduced supply during cold periods; the model indicates that temperature swings have a large and consistent impact on how many bikes customers want to rent hour by hour.
